name: Monochrome Modern
purpose: Create monochrome presentations with expressive serif titles, clear sans-serif information and deliberate tonal contrast. Adapt the composition to the content while preserving a recognisable typographic and spatial character.

logos.discovery: Search enabled sources at run time. Wikimedia Commons supplies structured candidates and metadata, while the official organization site or brand portal remains authoritative when available. Inspect the exact file and download the selected logo into the run cache with source URL, retrieval date, author, license or usage terms, attribution requirements, trademark notes, and checksum.
logos.fallback: If an exact official logo cannot be verified, pause and ask the user. Never substitute a generic symbol or reconstruct the logo from memory.

generic_icons.candidate_policy: Use a coherent Remix Icon line and fill pair when it can express the intended concept. Select the canonical variant after generated-slide approval through host-Agent visual review.
generic_icons.style: neutral monochrome, 24x24 optical footprint, line or fill selected per approved composition and peer group

asset_policy.photography: Use documentary, architectural, archival, or close-observation imagery. Prefer monochrome or naturally desaturated photographs with strong geometry and quiet human detail.
asset_policy.generated_visuals: Generated collage or abstract fields may remain raster when their texture, handwriting, paper grain, or photographic blending carries the meaning.

style.visual_language: Monochrome editorial typography with expressive serif titles, neutral sans-serif explanations, flat tonal fields, crisp rules and content-led composition. The references establish contrast and spacing relationships, not a fixed page layout.
style.whitespace: Separate distinct ideas and protect the dominant message while respecting the selected density. Avoid unnecessary empty areas on evidence-heavy pages.

modern_blocks.description: Near-white ground, dark serif display type, sans-serif evidence and square tonal fields where grouping helps. Layout follows the communication job.
modern_blocks.reconstruction: Favor native text, rectangles, rules, charts, tables, and continuous connectors. Photographs remain raster.

editorial_archive.description: Optional legacy variation for an explicit archival direction. Paper, handwriting and typewriter treatments are separate choices and do not belong to the default Monochrome Modern style.
editorial_archive.reconstruction: Rebuild title, labels, rules, major blocks, and semantic connectors natively. Preserve complex collage textures, handwriting, paper grain, and blended photography as one or more generated raster regions.

dark_editorial.description: Charcoal background, flat dark fields, off-white type, grayscale imagery, and quiet system-like precision.
dark_editorial.reconstruction: Use native dark fields and typography. Keep photographic material raster and avoid glow or glossy effects.

proxy_treatments.description: Thin neutral outline icon with no enclosing badge.
Off-white outline icon used directly on a dark field.

color: Use neutral monochrome for authored presentation elements. Preserve source colours in exact canonical assets when identity requires them.
geometry: Core information modules use square corners or an optically negligible radius.
Rounded media frames may use a restrained radius only when inherited from a photographed or embedded interface.
Avoid repeated floating cards. Build a composed page from fields, rules, blocks, and negative space.
composition: Each slide has one dominant statement or visual field.
Use asymmetry deliberately and balance it through scale, alignment, and empty space.
Use blocks to organize evidence. Do not imitate a product dashboard.
reconstruction: The Agent decides which visual regions carry irreducible texture and may remain raster.
Mechanical validation confirms package and geometry facts only. The Agent must visually compare the accepted image, measured overlay, rendered PowerPoint, and difference view before release.
Connector routes require an Agent-authored visual route decision. A script-generated route is only a candidate.

reconstruction_guidance.palette_authority: The accepted image supplies observed colours. Preserve quiet neutral and warm-grey variation within the monochrome direction. Exact canonical identity assets retain their source colours. Profile swatches are starting points for these tonal roles.
reconstruction_guidance.color_alignment: The host decides which objects intentionally share a color role. Sample interior pixels and inspect antialiasing, grain, shadows, transparency, and local contrast before selecting one shared color. Do not quantize photographs or paper texture globally.
reconstruction_guidance.font_authority: Reference font identities are uncertain. Use the declared available font roles, compare their appearance and preserve optical hierarchy. Any substitution must remain consistent across peer text.
reconstruction_guidance.typography: Preserve the chosen serif display and sans-serif explanatory roles. Verify recurring sizes, line breaks and tone in the render. Use archival voices only when the chosen mode explicitly calls for them.
reconstruction_guidance.raster_reuse: Prefer existing sharp crops at their intended display size. Preserve intrinsic lettering, layered paper, and background texture. Regenerate only when a specific quality or separation problem justifies it.

reasoning_principles: Infer the visual structure from the message. The light reference combines a large opening statement with a dense process, while the dark reference gives different weights to the statement and supporting explanation. Neither arrangement is a universal template.

Preserve the contrast between display type and explanatory type as information density changes. Balanced is a starting preference. A detailed slide can use the same visual language with more information and less empty space.
Choose light or dark treatment for a communication reason and hold that choice across related pages. Invert tonal roles coherently instead of introducing unrelated decoration.
Treat reference photographs as examples of framing and light. Their architecture, staircase subject and words are incidental and must not recur without a content reason.
visual_principles: Use a high-contrast serif for expressive titles and a neutral sans serif for explanations, diagram labels and evidence. Georgia and Arial are portable starting choices, not verified font identities from the references.

Let a small number of tonal roles establish emphasis. Near-black carries primary information on a near-white field, mid-grey supports it, and quiet rules or pale fields organise related material. Dark treatment reverses the foreground and background roles.
Organise content through shared alignments, text scale and proportion. Square fields and thin rules can clarify relationships without turning every group into a floating card.
Keep close spacing within related content and visibly greater separation between distinct ideas. Exact column counts, coordinates and box sizes follow each page.

Use flat backgrounds and clean edges for native content. Monochrome photographs may retain real texture and directional light when they explain or embody the subject. Avoid adding architectural stock imagery just to imitate the references.
Use canonical monochrome icons where they help identify a concept or asset. Keep the optical scale and stroke treatment consistent among peers and give them no compulsory badge.
Keep recurring labels and text roles consistent across a deck. A cover can use larger display type through an explicit role exception. Essential qualifications remain readable.
review_questions: Does the page retain the reference contrast between expressive titles and clear explanatory text?
Can the reader distinguish the main statement, supporting information and qualifications through tone and typography?
Does this composition explain the new content, or merely repeat a reference arrangement?
Do spacing and tonal fields express genuine groups at the requested density?
Are shared type roles and tonal meanings consistent in the actual PowerPoint renders?
Does each photograph, icon or other visual contribute to the message?
anti_patterns: Copying reference wording, personal-portfolio metadata, staircase imagery or its process labels into unrelated content.
Equating monochrome style with sparse content or forcing every page into the same asymmetric split.
Mixing handwriting, typewriter metadata and paper collage into the clean default direction without an explicit mode choice.
Using low-contrast grey for substantive text, or multiplying outlines and repeated dark label strips until the page becomes noisy.
Adding glows, bevels, glossy gradients, fake interface controls or decorative status symbols.
